meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief. Withdraw the zero on Owen's essay, and tell me why my son learned about it from a gradebook on his phone in the middle of class, and I didn't hear it from you.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Go on.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. Turn the screen so I can read it, and tell me what it is and what date is on it.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.
I'm writing down the times, Hale. Whose account is this history from, and does it show where those words came from, or only that they arrived? Turn the screen so I can read the page myself.
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.
In that one history, Hale. That tells me about one document, not about how my son works. Did you speak to Owen before you entered the zero, as your procedure 4.1 says you must?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

I asked you a question and you went around it, Hale. A student who changes his argument between an outline and an essay is revising, and that's what the course asks of him. I'm writing down October 15, and I want to read that outline myself.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

A misquoted line is an error, Hale, and it isn't a finding about who wrote it. I'm writing it down, and I'll search the play myself tonight. Show me where it sits in the essay, on the page, and then tell me whether Owen was asked about any of this before the zero went in.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Then stay there, Hale. You still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in. What are you proposing?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Give me a minute to read it. I'm writing down September 24. Then tell me what you say is different, in your own words, Hale.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.
I know what 4.4 says, Hale. I printed it. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, so is the zero still sitting in that gradebook where his classmates can see it?
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.

That answers where, Hale, and not the rest. I'll want it in an email from you tonight: the zero out of the gradebook today, and "nothing goes on file" in those words. Who else is in that room besides you?
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?
I'm not here to be comfortable, Hale. You have my terms: the zero out of the gradebook today, and an email from you tonight saying nothing goes on his file. Then we talk about a rewrite.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. I'm writing that down. The email covers one thing, though, and the zero comes out of the gradebook before you leave this building today, or I'm going to the principal's office.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
The date of the rewrite, who supervises it, that it's private, and that nothing goes on his file, all in your words. You also still haven't told me yes or no on the zero, Hale. I'm waiting.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Eight tonight, noted. That is a time for an email, Hale, and it isn't an answer about the zero. Say it plainly: does it come out today?
Thank you for coming in.
I'm still in this chair, Hale, and the zero hasn't been answered. Until it has, I'm not leaving, and the principal's office is next.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Tomorrow at lunch goes in your email, with the room and who supervises. That's still not an answer about the zero, Hale. You've now stepped around it four times, and I'm done asking politely.
